chapter_title: Learning Experience Design and Software Technology
title: Feedback Loops and Learner Control
description: AIL 606 textbook section connecting feedback loops and learner control to a feedback-loop specification (feed-forward text, reveal-timing rule, calibrated control, behavioral signal), reader notes, support moments, and revision evidence.
learning_objectives: Diagnose whether a practice loop feeds forward using Hattie and Timperley's three questions, and rewrite a bare verdict into actionable feedback.
Choose a feedback-reveal timing (immediate versus brief delay) justified by task type and learner expertise.
Design calibrated learner control that preserves autonomy while naming the cost of skipping.
Tie each loop revision to a behavioral signal such as repeat-error rate, skip rate, or retry uptake.
